instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: The error-strewn spell that cost him the Liverpool place; a fine shot-stopper with genuinely poor decision-making.
Joined Manchester City in January 2004; the seventeen starts are the half-season, not a drop in ability.
Thirty-five and first choice for a promoted Portsmouth side; the reflexes were undiminished and the England recall followed.
Moved to Newcastle in February 1998; the same player at both clubs.
Moved to Newcastle in February 1998; the same player at both clubs.
Peak years: a genuinely good all-round left midfielder, outstanding in the air for the position, but never an elite one.
Thirty-four and moved to Bolton; still an ever-present starter and outstanding in the air, but a level below the Newcastle years.
Thirty-seven and down to eleven starts; the engine and the aerial ability finally gone.
A converted forward at 18: an outstanding athlete, not yet a good top-flight defender. Rated as he was, not as he became.
Ever-present and an England starter at 21; the point at which he becomes a genuinely good defender.
Twenty-one starts in his last Tottenham season; a knee problem, not a decline.
Four seasons on and at his peak - the best centre-back in the division in the unbeaten season, and in the world conversation.
Sixteen starts: an achilles problem and the Old Trafford walk-off. Still an elite defender, a shade off the previous season.
The season that ended his Arsenal peak — the Highbury walk-off and a spell away from the club. Still a good defender, plainly not the 2003/04 one.
Rebuilt at Portsmouth: no longer quick enough to defend a high line, but still physically dominant and an excellent reader of a cross.
Thirty-four, ten starts, and back at Arsenal as a fourth-choice emergency centre-back.
Rated as the 18-year-old he was: first-choice wide man in a title side, not the finished player.
At his peak: among the best wide players in Europe in the treble season, even with the appearance total held down by hamstrings.
The PFA award this season was a career vote as much as a form one; he was still an excellent footballer, but a rotated one whose game had moved infield as the pace went.
Eighteen, three starts; a squad player, and rated as one.
Already the best midfielder at the club at 21, and still nine points short of the 2004/05 anchor (90).
Ever-present in a side that reached a Champions League semi-final; the late-arriving runs and the range of passing are both there, a rung below the 2004/05 anchor.
Twenty-two league goals in the double season is the biggest return of his career, but it is output — at thirty-one he was covering less ground than at the 2004/05 anchor and taking the penalties.
Outstanding before a cruciate injury ended his December.
Ankle broken and ligaments damaged in pre-season; returned in January visibly slower. He was not the same footballer again.
Rebuilt as a more static centre-forward: still powerful and a superb finisher, no longer the runner of 1995/96.
Knee trouble and two operations limited him to nineteen starts and five goals. Rated as the player, not the return.
Thirty-three, seven goals in twenty-six starts, and increasingly a static focal point rather than a threat in behind.
His last season, ended by a torn ligament in April. Ten goals as a static penalty-box centre-forward.
Rated as the 21-year-old Palace midfielder he was, not the England centre-back he became.
Converted to centre-back at Villa and immediately better there than he had been in midfield; England followed.
Captained a League Cup-winning side at 32; reading and organisation still excellent, the pace never having been the point.
Twenty-two starts after breaking a leg in September.
The season he became a centre-back for good, and immediately the best defender in a European Cup-winning side. A real step up rather than drift.
His peak: the best defender in a side that conceded 27 in the league and reached a second European Cup final in three years. Positionally close to flawless, never quick or comfortable in possession.
An ever-present in the Fulham side that finished seventh; thirty-five and still exactly the keeper he had been at Middlesbrough.
Ever-present as Newcastle finished fourth; quick off his line and an outstanding shot-stopper, if never commanding in his box.
Sold to Manchester City in February; the same goalkeeper at both clubs.
Sold to Manchester City in February; the same goalkeeper at both clubs.
Eighteen years old and already a 35-start centre-forward; rated as the raw power-and-pace forward he was, not the England career that followed.
A British record fee for a 21-year-old in March; the same player at both clubs.
Fourteen goals in the cup-treble season and an England starter at 22: the best football of his career, and the point where the power and pace were matched by end product.
Four goals in thirty-four starts as Birmingham went down; the physical game was still there, the end product of the Liverpool years was not.
Moved from Wigan to Aston Villa in January; the same player at both.
Moved from Wigan to Aston Villa in January; the same player at both.
Seventeen, eleven starts; obvious ability, obviously raw.
Twenty and already England’s most complete young defender; a long way short of the 2007/08 anchor (91) but clearly elite-bound.
A world record fee for a defender in November 2000; the same footballer at West Ham and Leeds, which is the point.
A world record fee for a defender in November 2000; the same footballer at West Ham and Leeds, which is the point.
Twenty starts: the eight-month ban for a missed drugs test began in January. Rated on the football, not on the availability.
His peak, and the docs anchor: a league and European Cup double conceding 22, with the pace to defend the high line and the passing to start attacks from it.
Twelve starts: the back trouble that shortened his career began here. Rated on the football, which was still excellent when he played.
Thirteen years on and playing central midfield at 35; still a competent top-half regular.
A 17-year-old holding down a top-flight place is remarkable, but the anchor is Barry at 26 (81). At 17 he was composed and positionally sound without the range he later had.
Eight assists from midfield at 22; the range and dead-ball delivery that define the 81 anchor at 26 are visibly arriving.
The docs anchor: good and dependable, a left-sided midfielder who could play anywhere across the middle without being outstanding at any of it.
Nine goals and ten assists as Villa finished sixth, and England’s first choice alongside Gerrard; the best season of his career, still short of elite.
Arguably the best English goalkeeper in the country in these Leeds seasons, and kept out of the England side rather than out of form.
Twenty-three starts: shared the Champions League season with Paul Robinson rather than lost form.
Thirty-six and the best goalkeeper at Everton by a distance; the two-season gap is a spell out of the side at Leeds, not a decline.
Thirty-eight and retired at the end of it with an ankle injury; still the better of Everton’s two keepers when fit.
Twenty years old, a double winner and an England starter at Euro 96 within months.
Peak Neville: positionally excellent and an intelligent defender, never an athletic or attacking outlier. Good rather than elite.
A broken foot in the spring; nineteen starts.
The missing season is a broken ankle and the eighteen months that followed it; he came back a slower, more limited full-back.
Nineteen, six starts, five goals — already an obvious top-flight footballer, not yet a starter.
A rung below the Keane anchor (91) in the same side and season; complete midfielder, not quite the driving force.
Fourteen league goals from midfield in a title season, and the best passer in the country. His peak.
Eighteen starts: the blurred-vision problem that nearly ended his career cost him from December. Rated as a diminished season rather than a decline.

Back fit and rebuilt as the deepest midfielder in a title-winning side — the role changes here because the player did: no longer the man arriving in the box, now the one setting the tempo from in front of the defence.
Inconsistent at Liverpool but a genuinely good goalkeeper; the Blackburn and Villa years show what the ability was.
Three years on from Liverpool and a different keeper: first choice all season for a Blackburn side that won the League Cup, and among the best in the division.
PFA Team of the Year; thirty-seven starts for a Blackburn side that finished sixth. His peak.
Thirty-seven and an ever-present for a Villa side that finished sixth; remarkably, no worse a goalkeeper than at thirty.
A poor, peripheral first season at United - seven starts and visibly short of confidence.
PFA and FWA Player of the Year at 34: fifteen goals from 23 starts and the link man in a title-winning side. A genuine late peak, not a reputation vote.
Thirty-seven at Portsmouth; the touch and the finishing remain, everything physical has gone.
Thirty-nine and six goals in fifteen starts; the reading of the game is all that is left, but it is genuinely still there.
Split between Newcastle and United by the January transfer; 21 league goals across the two.
Split between Newcastle and United by the January transfer; 21 league goals across the two.
A broken leg and then pneumonia; ten starts, and a player rebuilding rather than performing.
Nineteen goals in 23 starts, the best strike rate of his career, with the link play he had lacked earlier now present.
Fifteen starts as Sheringham and Solskjaer took the shirt; nine goals when he played.
Thirty-four and down to five starts across a season split between clubs.
Cruciate ruptured in September; nine starts. Rated as a good but half-fit player rather than on the peak either side of it.
The reinvention as a deeper, controlling midfielder: the treble season and the Juventus semi-final are the evidence.
Hip surgery in September cost him half the season and a good deal of his mobility; he came back a controlling midfielder rather than a driving one.
A broken foot in September, four starts, and a departure in November. He never played top-flight football again, and this is the shell of the 1999/00 anchor.
Thirty-nine, moved to Manchester City and retired in January with a shoulder injury. Visibly diminished in his last months.
Rated as the developing defender he was at 19, not the 100-cap international he became.
A regular in a Newcastle side that finished third, comfortable at centre-back or right-back; a good top-flight defender, still short of elite.
An ever-present in the Fulham defence that conceded 34 and finished seventh; his best sustained season, and still a good rather than elite defender.
Twenty-one and in and out of the side.
On loan at Newcastle in his first English season; quick and raw.
Two consecutive ever-present seasons as City’s captain; among the quickest and most physically imposing centre-backs in the division.
Thirty-seven starts as City’s captain; the pace and the physique made him a genuinely difficult centre-back to play against, if never a composed one on the ball.
Moved to Everton in August after three appearances for Portsmouth; the same defender at both.
Moved to Everton in August after three appearances for Portsmouth; the same defender at both.
Thirty-eight and down to sixteen starts in a West Ham side that went down.
Twenty years old and in and out of the side.
First full season as a starter; quick, powerful and clearly a level up from the fringe player of the year before.
A British record fee for a defender in October 2000; the same player Villa sold, which is the point.
Nine starts at 31; injuries, and Southgate and Riggott ahead of him.
Twenty and already a first-choice wide player, though a raw one.
Settled at West Ham as a direct, two-footed wide player; the level that eventually took him to a World Cup.
Stepped straight into the champions’ midfield at 20 when Ince was sold.
His best year: with Keane injured for stretches he was United’s most reliable central midfielder, and he carried that form into England’s 2002 World Cup.
Twelve starts; squeezed out by Keane, Scholes and the emerging Fletcher.
A poor first season at Newcastle — injured early, never fluent, and visibly a step slower.
On loan at Birmingham and relegated with them; twenty-two starts of honest, unremarkable holding midfield.
Back at Newcastle and fit, which the 2004/05 season was not; a small recovery rather than an improvement in the player.
A clean, positionally sound full-back and Wimbledon's captain; the ceiling is low but the floor is high.
Eighteen and raw: obviously talented, but four starts of a player still well short of what he became.

The breakthrough season — twenty-six starts at nineteen, physically ready and driving, with an England call-up at the end of it. The jump on the previous year is real development, not a re-reading of the same player.

Twenty-nine starts and seven goals in the treble season; the physical power, passing range and shooting were all in place at twenty. A five-point rise on the breakthrough year, which is real development at that age.
Captain of a European Cup-winning side and the driving force of it; a rung below the Lampard anchor (90) on league-long consistency, Liverpool having finished fifth.
World class by twenty-five: ten league goals, the FA Cup final he won on his own, and the complete range of passing, shooting and driving running.

His peak, and one of the outstanding individual seasons of the era — sixteen goals and nine assists from behind Torres as Liverpool took 86 points. In the conversation for the best midfielder in the world.
A groin problem carried all season and a side that fell to seventh; visibly a level below the year before.
A composed, athletic keeper at 23 in a side that finished seventh; already close to international standard.
An ever-present for a Villa side that finished sixth; the best sustained season of his career.
The docs anchor: a regular 90s starter, below modern standard, aged 19.
His peak by a distance: ever-present, nine goals, and the driving force of a Champions League semi-finalist at 23. Nine points above the 1996/97 anchor across four seasons of real improvement.
Four starts at thirty-one and out of the West Ham side entirely.
Thirty-four starts for a Birmingham side that finished ninth; fit and first choice again, which is why the number recovers slightly rather than the player improving.
Sixteen years old and physically ready for the division, which is why he played; the reading of the game came much later.
Sold to Manchester City in October; the same player at both clubs.
Sold to Manchester City in October; the same player at both clubs.
City’s player of the year and an ever-present; the reading of the game had finally caught up with the physique.
Thirty-five starts as Villa finished sixth and a fourth City player-of-the-year behind him; slow and limited on the ball, but a genuinely good defender of his own box.
PFA Team of the Year at 21; quick, aggressive and increasingly a genuine attacking threat.
Eight starts before the knee trouble that put him out of football entirely for a season.
A year without a club and then thirty-five starts for a Birmingham side that finished ninth; the pace has gone but the defending has not.
Thirty-six starts for a Bolton side that finished sixth; a superb shot-stopper and one of the better keepers in the division across these years.
Nineteen and a fringe player.
Straight into the side as an FA Cup-winning starter; the step is a real change in the player, not a re-rating.
Thirty-two and splitting a season between two clubs off the bench; the last of him as a top-flight player.
Thirty-two and splitting a season between two clubs off the bench; the last of him as a top-flight player.
The 74 anchor is Davies at 32, when the physical game that got him an England cap was fully formed. At 20-22 he was a quick, raw forward and a worse player than the anchor.
One goal in twenty-one starts back at Southampton; the low point of his career.

Rebuilt at Bolton as the physical focal point of the side — a genuinely different player from the quick young forward of 1997/98, which is why the role appears only from here. An ever-present with nine goals and nine assists.
The docs anchor: thirty-two, an England cap, and the physical hold-up game fully formed. Plainly below a modern Premier League starter, but a squad player in one.
Loaned to Derby in January and relegated with them; the same player at both clubs, and visibly the end of him at this level.
Loaned to Derby in January and relegated with them; the same player at both clubs, and visibly the end of him at this level.
Captain of the title winners; a good, disciplined midfielder rather than a technically special one.
Joined Tottenham in February 1999.
Joined Tottenham in February 1999.
Ever-present at 19 and straight into the Ireland World Cup squad; unusually finished for his age, and he did not improve much on it.
Wenger's arrival turned a squad player into a first-choice one; the double season is where he becomes genuinely good.
Ten years on from the previous season here: a mature, England-capped midfielder rotating through the unbeaten Arsenal side.
Thirty-two and down to eleven starts at Middlesbrough; the last of him in the top flight.
